newsitem.title: LEBANON: Byblos Bank listing on Beirut exchange delayed.
newsitem.headline: Byblos Bank listing on Beirut exchange delayed.

text.p: Listing of Byblos Bank shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange has been slightly delayed by a minor legal issue, a source close to the bank said on Friday.

He said the bank was seeking a way to reconcile a legal requirement that one-third of its shares must be owned by Lebanese citizens with the fact that shares it puts on the market can be bought by foreigners.
At present only one-third of Byblos' shares are owned by Lebanese, the source said.
The issue was under discussion with the central bank, he said.
"It can't take too long now. I guess the bank will take a decision soon on how to do it and I personally think the shares will be traded by March," he added.

Byblos shares, which are keenly awaited on the market, had been expected to start trading at the end of January or early February. They would be the third bank shares on the exchange following recent listings by Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce and Banque Audi.

Market sources consider Byblos Bank well and aggressively run. They say its shares have risen to $4.25 from $2.60 on the grey market in Beirut over the past two years and demand is currently very strong.
